tasks.short: Examine theory for improved statistical methods

steps.what: Examine probability and inference theories, develop arguments and test proposed mathematical methods

tasks.design: Keep theoretical examination and derivation with the statistician, using {DOCS} and existing computational support in {DATA_PLATFORM}. A generated argument is not accepted as a proof or a demonstrated labour reduction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Discovering a valid mathematical basis requires original reasoning and verification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing symbolic and numerical tools can support expert investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Finding hidden assumptions and proving claims beyond tested examples.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising why an argument works and where it fails.
tasks.altitude: Theoretical responsibility and research time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Relevant proof techniques and mathematical literature

evidence.claim: Numerical experiments alone cannot establish general mathematical validity; no task-specific saving is demonstrated here.

assumptions: Boundary covers theoretical examination and method derivation, excluding production data processing and routine reporting.
Statistician produces definitions, assumptions, conjectures and checks within s1; no structured proof-validity flag is assumed.
Consider native symbolic and numerical tools before custom code; no additional system is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing research process is retained.
unknowns: Share of work in reusable symbolic manipulations
research_questions: Can measured examples separate repetitive manipulation from original argument and verification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Existing computational support is already in the baseline; proof and discovery time remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise data collection and tabulation workers

steps.what: Prepare instructions for workers collecting and tabulating data
Supervise workers, explain instructions and resolve collection or tabulation problems

tasks.design: Keep instructions in {DOCS} and retain personal supervision through the existing communication channels. No automatic quality or worker status feed is assumed, and no repeated clerical component has been established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions and supervision depend on study-specific collection problems.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared documents provide a common instruction version.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether workers understand the protocol and resolving ambiguous cases.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching practical interpretation and noticing systematic misunderstandings.
tasks.altitude: Supervisory authority and working time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Improve collection instructions and escalation examples
reach.learn: Domain-specific collection procedures and query handling

evidence.claim: Supervision combines study-specific instruction and contextual problem resolution; no labour reduction is established.

assumptions: Boundary includes instruction preparation and supervision, excluding workers' collection labour and separate statistical data-quality assessment.
Workers raise questions and observations during existing supervision; the statistician reads and resolves them in s2. No newly structured progress or discrepancy feed is required.
Test native document sharing and communication features before custom code; no new automation is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the current instruction and supervision process remains unchanged.
unknowns: Whether repeated administrative reminders consume measurable supervision time
research_questions: Do supervision logs show repeated reminders that can be separated from instruction and problem solving?

incremental.description: No new system upkeep or worker capture requirements

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Instruction and supervision retain full time; no free structured worker reporting is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Specify data warehouses, including table grain, keys, types and access requirements
Prepare warehouse table definitions and standard loading scaffolds from the approved specification
Test warehouse structures, review permissions and apply the approved change package

tasks.design: Generate standard table definitions and loading scaffolds in {DATA_PLATFORM} from a statistician-owned structure specification. Keep semantic design, permission checks, migration testing and deployment approval with authorized people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated definitions and standard loading scaffolds require mechanical transcription after design choices are settled.
tasks.enabler_now: Schema-driven generators can render explicit definitions without choosing data meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Correct grain, keys, historical changes, access boundaries and safe migration.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding which warehouse structure preserves the meaning of the data.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time typing standard definitions and retain responsibility for structure correctness.

reach.task: Specify warehouse changes with explicit contracts
reach.learn: Dimensional modelling, access control and migration testing

evidence.claim: Explicit schema metadata can drive deterministic table-definition and scaffold generation; the proposed saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers preparing warehouse structures, not original source collection, analytical method design or continuing warehouse operations.

Statistician produces table grain, column names and types, nullability, keys, joins, source mapping, retention and requested access in s1, including capture time. Access decisions follow existing authorization; no inferred permission flag is accepted.

Test native schema generation and migration tools first. Incomplete specifications or unsupported migrations require manual definitions and testing; the generator never invents joins or access rights.

Only repetitive human definition writing is removed; existing generated definitions and database runtime earn no saving. Statistician must have existing deployment authority; otherwise the authorized administrator's unchanged deployment remains outside this boundary.
unknowns: Statistician's actual deployment authority and warehouse responsibilities
research_questions: How much standard definition typing remains after native generation and required migration review are counted?

already_counted.description: Validation, permission review and deployment approval

incremental.description: Generator access and platform compatibility maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact schema and migration package, permission set, tests and target environment; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65, gross35 minus focal upkeep10 gives net25. Range allows already-generated definitions, complex migrations and uncommon schemas to absorb most or all benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retains theoretical and supervisory responsibilities while reducing repetitive warehouse definition work where present.
reach: Work with database architects on explicit warehouse change contracts
role.ambitious_version: Use measured scaffold-writing gains to strengthen warehouse correctness and reproducibility.
